title: Moving a grow light moves what grows under it
question: The only change between these two is which column one fixture is bolted at. Does the bed read as being lit by the lamps now — and is the difference big enough to be worth dragging one?
context_md:
The lab had a ceiling **and** a sky, and the sky was doing the work: four rows of stone pass 0.447 of full daylight, which was the crop's entire light budget, and replacing every fixture with plain stone left the stand byte-identical. So the picture said grow lights and the physics said sunshine through the roof.

The box is now sunless and the fixtures are the light. Each one throws a pool straight down its own column, so **where a lamp sits decides what thrives under it** — and dragging one off a plant station kills that plant.

Both beds are the same seed, same founders, same 3,600 frames. In **B** the leftmost fixture has been dragged 84 columns to the right, into the next bay. Its founder dies; nothing else was touched.

Two things I am unsure of and would rather you told me:

- **The pool is visible on the back wall but not on the ground.** The bench light is real — the plants respond to it — but the renderer only reads it near the ceiling, so the bright patch you can see is the backdrop rather than the ground. Making the ground show it is a small change in a file another lane is rewriting this week. Worth doing?
- **The bed is dimmer between lamps than it was.** That is the mechanic working, but it may have gone too far.

items.label: A — fixtures as built, one over each plant station
items.caption: eight fixtures, evenly spread; every founder has a light over it

items.label: B — the leftmost fixture dragged into the next bay
items.caption: one lamp moved 84 columns right; nothing else changed
